This page covers the **folium** template settings, contributors, custom files, branding, and extensions. For general Quarto syntax, see [Demo Report](demo.qmd). To start a report, use [Report](report.qmd).

## Project setup

Update these `_quarto.yml` fields when starting a project:

| Key | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `nbis.id` | NBIS support request ID, such as `"2222"`. Used in the default subtitle and `report.qmd`. |
| `website.site-url` | Public URL of the site. |
| `website.favicon` | Browser tab icon. |
| `website.navbar.logo` | Navbar logo. |
| `format.html.title-block-banner` | Page title banner. |
| `format.html.image` | Default featured image; pages can override it. |
| `website.image` | Social preview image. |

Any site-wide default in `_quarto.yml` can be overridden in a page's YAML frontmatter. Common options are:

- `toc`, `number-sections`, and `number-depth` control navigation and numbering.
- `code-fold`, `code-tools`, and `code-copy` control code blocks.
- `date` and `date-format` control page dates. Use `date: ""` to hide the date.
- `subtitle` overrides the default `"NBIS Support {{< meta nbis.id >}}"`.
- `execute` controls code evaluation, output, warnings, and caching.

The sidebar automatically lists files matching `reports/*`. To manage links manually, remove `website.sidebar` from `_quarto.yml` and add links to `index.qmd`.

`completion.qmd` contains standard NBIS completion text and normally does not need editing. To hide it until the project is finished, add this to `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
project:
  render:
    - "*.qmd"
    - "!completion.qmd"
```

Use `reports/report.qmd` as the starting point for a support report. It includes a version history and sections for setup, methods, deliverables, summary, conclusion, and session information. Use `##` for top-level body headings because `#` is reserved for the page title.

## Authors and metadata

The top-level `author` in `_quarto.yml` applies to every page. Use `author: ""` on a page to hide it. Multiple authors can be listed:

```
author: 
  - "Person A"
  - "Person B"
```

The custom `contributors` key lists people who worked on the project:

| Field | Notes |
|---|---|
| `name` | Required. Entries without a name and duplicate names are skipped. |
| `email` | Optional email link. |
| `affiliation` | Optional string or list. |
| `roles` | Optional string or list. Missing roles appear under **Contributor**. |

Display all contributors with:

{{< contributors >}}

Filter by role with positional arguments or `roles=`. Matching is case-insensitive:

```
::: {.callout-note}
{{{< contributors analyst pi >}}}
:::
```

::: {.callout-note}
{{< contributors analyst pi >}}
:::

People matching several roles appear under each role. Contributor styles use `.quarto-contributors-*` classes in `assets/css/styles.scss`.

**Computed metadata.** A custom Lua filter (`assets/custom.lua`) adds metadata such as `quarto_version`, `current_date`, `current_year`, `current_time`, `output-dir`, and `output-dir-path`. [Demo Report → Shortcodes](demo.qmd#shortcodes) shows live examples. Selected `_quarto.yml` values are available under `custom.*`, for example `` `{{{< meta custom.website.site-url >}}}` ``.

::: {.callout-caution}
`{{{< meta custom.* >}}}` supports only simple scalar values under `project`, `website`, and `format`. Lists, flow-style values, and block scalars render as `[unsupported yaml]`.
:::

## Styling and extensions

Two files control the site's appearance:

- **`assets/include_head.html`** loads fonts and prevents search indexing with `<meta name="robots" content="noindex">`. Remove that line to make a published site discoverable.
- **`assets/css/styles.scss`** defines the colors, fonts, and custom classes:
  - Font-size spans: `.largest`, `.larger`, `.large`, `.small`, `.smaller`, `.smallest`
  - Buttons: `.btn-primary`, `.btn-secondary`, `.btn-tertiary` (combine with Quarto's own `.btn`)
  - Badges: `.badge-primary`, `.badge-secondary`, `.badge-tertiary` (combine with `.badge`)
  - `.contents-table` for compact tables
  - `.fourofour` for the custom 404 heading

The theme also styles Quarto's standard callouts.

Three Quarto extensions are bundled under `_extensions/`:

- **`quarto-ext/fontawesome`** and **`royfrancis/accordion`** are demonstrated in [Demo Report](demo.qmd).
- **`mcanouil/collapse-output`** makes code output collapsible:

  ```{{python}}
  #| output-fold: true
  #| output-summary: "Click to view"
  ```

  `output-summary` is optional and defaults to `"Code Output"`.

For a fresh template without the committed `_extensions/` directory, install them once:

```
quarto add quarto-ext/fontawesome
quarto add mcanouil/quarto-collapse-output@1.4.0
quarto add royfrancis/quarto-accordion
```

## Building and publishing

- `quarto preview` previews the full site.
- `quarto preview reports/usage.qmd` previews one page.
- `quarto render reports/usage.qmd` renders one page.
- `quarto render` builds the site in `docs/`.
